parts.lead:
VR headset from HP with four 640×480 grayscale tracking cameras and an IMU at about 1 kHz. All four are solved from the Monado SLAM calibration data, in three pair recordings stitched together.

parts.glance:
VR headset from HP with four 640×480 grayscale tracking cameras and an IMU at about 1 kHz. All four are solved from the Monado SLAM calibration data, in three pair recordings stitched together.

Reprojection median0.13 px
cam0–cam1 baseline108.5 mm
cam0 td−1.25 ms
cam0 lever arm53.8 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

One recording shown, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

parts.limits:
• One recording shown, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
  • This rig is stitched from three solves, not one joint solve. Cameras seen in two pairs agree to 0.89 mm and 0.34° (cam0) and 0.54 mm and 0.15° (cam1). cam2 and cam3 move 0.79 and 0.52 mm depending on how they are attached.
  • The process figure and values for the IMU show the cam0 + cam1 recording only.
parts.run: • Each recording shows the board to one camera pair, so three pairs are solved: cam0 + cam1, cam0 + cam2, cam1 + cam3. Each is camera + IMU with camera intrinsics free and t_ga estimated, on current MVIS, 2026-11-03. cam0, cam1 and all IMU values come from the first pair. cam2 is attached through cam0 and cam3 through cam1.

parts.detail:
Lens Calibrated field of view

Calibrated field of view, horizontal × vertical. cam0: 118° × 94°, corners reach 65° from the axis · cam1: 119° × 95°, corners reach 69° from the axis · cam2: 118° × 94°, corners reach 67° from the axis · cam3: 118° × 94°, corners reach 64° from the axis

cam0 cam1 cam2 cam3

We read these from the calibrated lens fit at the image edges, through the principal point (where the optical axis meets the image). ~ marks an axis past where the corners reached, so the fit is extrapolated there. Past the fit means an edge lies beyond where the fit holds, so we give no value.

IMU Gyro–accel time offset t_ga +2.54 ms

Each bar shows a scale as its deviation from 1. IMU model: calyx. t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and accelerometer channels: +2.54 ± 0.20 ms.
